judgment.rationale: A Command Palette collaborator confirmed that the Dock remains an AppBar-style docked window when always-on-top is disabled and that auto-hide, not this toggle, is the intended way to reclaim the reserved screen area.
evidence: The report covers PowerToys 0.100.2, installed via PowerToys auto-update, affecting Command Palette.
Reported reproduction: 1. Activate Command Palette 2. Activate Dock 3. Tick "Always at the foreground" off

Reported result: The Dock stays at the foreground regardless of the parameter state, and the screen real estate of the entire Dock is reserved for it, making it impossible for windows to be completely fullscreen. Plus, when dragging a window to the top of the screen, the window layout UI is truncated by the Dock, making it unusable.

Expected result: Because the option is ticked off, any window should be able to placed on top of the Dock, and dragging a window to the top of the screen should make the application full screen, thus hiding the Dock

Latest public comment by @jiripolasek on 2026-06-30T11:17:25Z: Hi, that's intended behavior: the toggle does disable always-on-top behavior, but the Dock is still a docked window and behaves as such. Dock auto-hide feature will be available in the next version.
